about: Fault counts the gates in tool/ are held to. Read by tool/check_gates.py, which fails when a gate's count moves in either direction: up means a new fault, down means a baseline that should be lowered so the repair sticks. 'measured' is the date the count last changed. Regenerate with `python3 tool/check_gates.py --update`; write 'note' by hand.

check_barrel_exports.note: Lands at zero because all four faults it found were legitimate omissions, and each was declared with a marker in its barrel in the same pass: reflection_seed.dart in advanced_client_core, reflection_entry.dart in todo_domain, and the two generated colour/icon tables behind tom_colors.dart and tom_icons.dart in tom_flutter_ui. Zero is the expected steady state -- the gate exists for recurrence, not backlog, and the one defect of this class (session_two_factor_controller.dart, absent from advanced_app_client's app.dart) was already repaired by tcinc947. 39 barrels across 23 packages are in scope. A directory with no barrel is deliberately not covered: the six Flutter sample applications correctly re-export nothing from screens/ and groups/, and demanding it would produce some ninety faults, all wrong.

check_comments_read_as_is.note: 21 history-narration phrases, all outside the five tom_core packages: 16 in tom_flutter_ui, 4 in tom_flutter_form_test, 1 in tom_flutter_ui_test -- see tcextension11_aidb. Zero work-item ids remain anywhere in scope. This gate covers what check_section_refs.py does not: quest todo ids, build-plan ids, 'Todo <n>' pointers and past-indicative narration about the code's own history. It matches ids by *shape* against a closed vocabulary of English and published technical words, in both lowercase and ALL-CAPS; it does not enumerate quest prefixes, because a prefix list fails open -- minting a new one defeats it silently, which is how 104 ALL-CAPS pointers in 18 families shipped past a green gate.

check_dartdoc_build.note: Zero, and held there. `dart doc` must report neither a warning nor an error for tom_core_kernel, tom_core_agentic or tom_core_codespecs. Every fault is one bracketed name in one comment, so a rise of one is a real regression rather than noise -- this count was 11 for tom_core_kernel alone before the gate existed.

check_doc_ai_citations.note: Lands at zero because the two faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass. Both were in tom_flutter_ui/doc/ and both cited _ai/quests/flutter_ui/acl_json_layout.md; one of them, under 'Separation with json-Acl-layout', called that document the canonical layout contract, so a shipped document deferred its authority to a file its reader cannot obtain. The cited file exists, which is what makes this class of defect survive a scan: neither find nor git ls-files follows the _ai symlink, so the citation reads as 'file does not exist' to any tool run from the container root. Keying on the citation rather than on the target is what makes the answer stable. _copilot_guidelines/, CHANGELOG.md and tool/ are out of scope because _ai/ is genuinely reachable for their readers.

check_doc_artifacts.note: One artifact deliberately left tracked: tom_core_kernel/doc/analyzer_analysis.json (13.3 MB), held open by tcfinal8_aidb, whose pending decision asks whether the artefact is still wanted at all. Unlike the six files this gate was written for -- three doc/last_testrun.json captures and three doc/baseline_*.csv, all removed in the same pass -- it is regenerated deliberately and referenced by tooling, so removing it here would pre-empt the user's decision. Lower this to 0 when that decision lands as removal.

check_doc_attributions.note: Clean. 441 attribution claims, 105 type names judged. The one fault found on the first run (tom_flutter_ui_test's layout table calling lib/locale_settings.dart an AppBar language selector) was repaired in the same pass, so a rise here is a new misattribution, not a backlog.

check_doc_class_inventories.note: Zero is the steady state, not an untested gate: the 81 stale (TBD) markers, the 42 names that named nothing, and the 3 shipped classes the appendix never mentioned were all repaired in the pass that introduced the checker, so it is baselined on a document it has already moved. One marked region, over tom_flutter_ui/lib/src/forms/fields, holding 97 classes of the TomField hierarchy. `--self-test` perturbs that region by one name in each direction and requires MISSING and PHANTOM to fire, so a zero here still means the checker is reading.

check_doc_dart_blocks.note: Lands at zero because the 14 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass, across 11 tom_core_kernel documents. Zero here does not mean the tree is clean: only tom_core_kernel is in PACKAGES, and doc/api_reference/ is excluded within it. tom_core_server reports 19 when run with its name as an argument, tom_flutter_ui and tom_core_flutter have not been surveyed -- see tcextension7_aico-doc-dart-blocks-other-packages.

check_doc_dependencies.note: Lands at zero because the 28 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass. Eleven of the 15 package completion documents carried a Dependencies section and seven of those were incomplete; the four remaining package documents (advanced_app_server, advanced_auth_server, advanced_ops_server, core_server_sample) had no section at all and were written, so a missing section is a NOSECTION fault rather than a skip -- a gate you can pass by deleting the section is not a gate. Every one of the 28 omissions was a build-time entry (build, build_runner, tom_reflection_generator, lints, test, flutter_test, flutter_lints) while the runtime half was complete in every case. Module documents are skipped: a document is audited only when its opening inventory resolves to a directory carrying a pubspec.yaml.

check_doc_error_keys.note: One key listed in an "Error keys" section that no code raises: `storage.blob.exists` in tom_core_server_file_storage_new.md. The count survived a widening from 3 audited documents to 9: the gate now also reads a package document anchored on its opening `tom_*/...` path, its key literals in camelCase as well as snake_case, and `Error(`/`errorKey:` raise sites beside `Exception(`. That widening surfaced 8 keys the sample documents raised and never named -- three `app.*.invalid` in advanced_app_server, three `admin.*.not_found` and two `login.error.2fa.no-*` in advanced_auth_server -- all documented in the same pass, which is why the number did not move.

check_doc_inventories.note: Zero because all 94 faults were repaired by `--fix` in one pass. The repair was forced: the repo-wide `dart format` of tcincb1_ahti reflowed 777 Dart files, and an INDEX/HEADER/LINES claim is measured against the module's source line totals, not against the wording of the document -- so the reflow invalidated 46 figures on top of the 48 already stale here. `--fix` cannot repair only the 46: a figure is right or wrong, so the same pass also discharged the 48 that tcfinal1_aicl_stale_module_header_figures owned. 33 documents, 90 substitutions, every line identical in length before and after, so no line needed re-wrapping. Adding or retiring a table row still needs a hand, because a new row needs a sentence saying what the file carries. Still zero after the LAYOUT widening, which checks every layout-tree row's file for existence rather than only the rows that also claim a length: 264 rows across 16 documents, all present, and one more document audited (tom_core_samples_assets_new.md, whose drawn tree of 9 SVGs is the only inventory it has). Still zero after the PROSE widening, which reports a length figure sitting in a position no other audit read. It is instrumented rather than pattern-matched: each audit records the spans it took a length out of and PROSE reports the leftovers, so the census and index sentences -- prose, but read -- stay covered and widening any audit narrows PROSE automatically. It found 28 unchecked measurements across 14 documents, including `Eight steps, one file, 239 lines` of a file that had been 250 for four commits; all 28 were removed by rewriting the sentence rather than by restating the number, since a length nothing maintains is worse than no length. `--fix` does not repair PROSE: the number is usually right and what is wrong is where it sits.

check_doc_links.note: Lands at zero because the 90 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass: 84 ABSOLUTE links to /_copilot_guidelines/ in the 14 _copilot_guidelines/ files of this repo, 4 DEAD ../tom_core_*/ links written one level too shallow in the kernel's and server's index.md, 1 DEAD api_summary_result.md for a Result module the kernel does not have, and 1 GUIDELINE link out of tom_flutter_ui/README.md. The ABSOLUTE shape was workspace-wide -- 371 links in 70 files across tom_ai, tom_assistant, tom_sqm, tom_uam and the global _copilot_guidelines/ -- all repaired in the same pass, and its source, the index.md template in _copilot_guidelines/dart/new_project_setup.md, was corrected so the count stops growing by one table per new project. Anchors are out of scope (check_doc_tocs owns headings) and so are external URLs.

check_doc_samples.note: 8 miscalled constructors in two tom_flutter_ui documents -- five TomForm* samples passing a named argument to a constructor whose first parameter is positional, and three TomColumn samples passing positionally to a named-only constructor. The count is unchanged across two widenings that each landed clean, which is the fact worth recording: the corpus grew from 192 documents and 1802 fences to 257 and 3432 when the quest's 79 completion documents came into scope, and the SIGNATURE fault began checking quoted declarations that were previously skipped. Neither found a live defect -- the one the gate was extended for, TomListForm documented and called positionally in tom_flutter_ui_forms_changes.md, had been repaired in the meantime -- and both were confirmed to fire by putting the defect back. A 'documents unplaced' line is now printed at every run: 13 tom_core_samples READMEs and the completion index, none of which names a single package, and all of which were silently skipped before.

check_doc_tocs.note: Zero is the steady state. The gate now covers every in-document anchor, not only the ones a table of contents uses: check_doc_links accepts any #fragment and names this gate as the one that decides whether the heading exists, so a [§10](#stale-anchor) in running prose is this gate's fault to report. 253 documents are scanned for that; 117 of them carry a table of contents and are additionally held to listing every ## section, in document order. The four faults are exercised by planting each in a real document and requiring it to fire.

check_member_attributions.note: Lands at zero because every fault it found on its first repo-wide run was repaired in the same pass. The subject was tom_flutter_ui_test/doc/widget_resource_parameters.md, whose resolver table named seven methods that existed nowhere and attributed the rest to TomNodeBase, which declares no resolvers; the 1,181 references were requalified onto TomCtr and TomStyleResolvers, the types the widgets actually call. That exposed eight more across four other documents, each a single wrong name -- TomTotp2FAService.encodeBase32 for generateSecret, TomBool.value for get(), TomFormStyle.requiredIndicator for the field it is declared on, TomAclBuilder.setBpMinWidth for addRowBreakpoint, TomField.formName/fieldName for TomForm.formId and TomField.tomId, and TomDbType.of for the of() the subclasses carry. A rise means a document now names a member its type does not declare; a fall means a member was deleted or renamed and the baseline should follow it down.

check_section_refs.note: Zero, and held there. Every shipped lib/, test/ and example/ comment either says what it means in its own words or names the document its section number belongs to -- in practice always doc/acl_design_specification.md or doc/tom_ui_list_forms.md, both of which ship with the package. A bare '§7.2' or 'Phase 2a §16' indexes a quest plan that ships with neither the package nor its tests, so a reader of the shipped artefact cannot resolve it; the next one to arrive is a failure. Zero means something only because the gate also refuses the *marked* form -- 'bug §77', 'tests §61(e)' -- outright, before it asks whether a document is in view. Proximity cannot judge that shape: a comment may open with a pointer into a backlog and go on to cite a real document two lines below, and the citation would otherwise vouch for the pointer. Naming a work item is naming something the reader cannot open, so it is a fault whatever else is on the page.

check_shared_chrome.note: Zero from the day it landed, which took six repairs. Eight groups of file are copied between packages on purpose -- the four showcase samples' chrome, the DTO reflection helpers, the client-local login credentials -- and every copy now names its whole group in its header comment. Two demo_box.dart copies named each other and not the third, so a developer editing either was told about one other copy out of two; two further groups were identical in code and declared nowhere at all. Both halves of the rule earn their place: the declaration carries showcase_cell.dart's fourth copy, which has drifted in code, and content discovery found the two groups no declaration mentioned. The next copy to arrive undeclared, or the next pointer to fall out of step with its siblings, is a failure.

check_source_citations.note: Holds at zero across a scope that widened twice. Markdown was first excluded outright (173 citations in tom_core_samples), then admitted for that subtree once they had been rewritten by hand to name declarations, and now covers every document that navigates -- doc/ pages, package READMEs and the sample guides, 177 files against the previous 39. The widening cost twelve repairs, nine of them in doc/ pages shipped to consumers, and one was the class of failure this gate exists for: form_authorizers.md cited tom_authorization.dart:352 for `class TomAuthorizer`, which is a doc comment belonging to a different class eighty lines above it -- resolving, fluent and wrong. Three sites named their target and cited a line as well, and one cited `(line 151)` into a file that had since been deleted; both are the argument against validating the numbers rather than removing them. CHANGELOGs, _copilot_guidelines/ and the repo's own README stay out, each for a stated reason rather than a suppression entry -- the last so the suite can go on quoting the shapes it forbids.

check_tooling_table.note: Lands at zero because the two faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass: check_unimplemented_claims.py and this gate itself were on disk with no row in the README tooling table and no prose section. Zero is the expected steady state -- the gate exists for recurrence, not backlog. The drift it guards had already re-opened once: check_kernel_bridge.py and check_section_numbers.py were filed as missing, were added incidentally before the filing was worked, and a third script had silently taken their place by then.

check_unimplemented_claims.note: Lands at zero because the nine faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass: two copies of one `Implemented: No` table, in tom_ui_flutter_widgets.md and tom_ui_widgets_forms.md, each denying nine widgets that had shipped months earlier.
